headline: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 709 as 7 children die in 24 hours
summary: Four infants died at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital on Friday, bringing the facility's death toll to 58.
details: A severe measles outbreak in Bangladesh has seen the national death toll rise to 709. In a single 24-hour window, seven children succumbed to the disease.
Four of those deaths occurred at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH), where the total number of deaths has reached 58. All four infants who died on Friday were aged 8 months or younger.
The victims included children from Mymensingh, Netrokona, and Sunamganj. Since the outbreak began on March 17, MMCH has admitted 2,378 children, with 2,226 having recovered.

Associate Professor Golam Mawla of the paediatrics department noted that the deceased children suffered from other illnesses alongside measles. He highlighted that most had not been breastfed, leaving them with weakened immune systems.

headline: Smartphone prices may rise by 20-25% from July 1
summary: A temporary 15% import duty waiver expires on June 30, potentially pushing up retail prices for imported mobile phones.
details: Imported smartphone prices in Bangladesh could jump by 20% to 25% starting July 1, as a temporary import duty waiver expires. The interim government had provided a 15% duty reduction in January, which is set to end on June 30.
caption:
Thinking of buying a new smartphone? You might have to pay thousands more if you wait until July.

Imported smartphone prices in Bangladesh could jump by 20% to 25% starting July 1, as a temporary import duty waiver expires. The interim government had provided a 15% duty reduction in January, which is set to end on June 30.
